title: D6 p6b: native offline keybindings-draft probe and store-free discard
body:
Stacked on #1900 (p6a); diff against main includes it and #1808 until they merge. Second of three pieces #1791 (p6) is decomposed into.

## What this piece delivers
Wires p6a's read-outcome primitives into the native app's actual offline recovery feature:

- The real Storage-backed backend (`NativePreferencesProvider.tsx`) routes its `get()`/`matches()` through `parseDraftBytes`/`matchesStoredBytes` so a stored JSON null or bytes this build cannot parse classify as an unreadable RECORD, not a dead port or a silent "no draft".
- A cold-offline probe (`useEffect` on `[hubId, state]`) classifies the local record via `readDraftOutcome` before any model publishes a snapshot - `bindNativePreferences`'s `ready` callback never fires on a cold offline start, so this is the only signal the "Discard unreadable draft" action has to render on.
- `discardUnreadableKeybindingsDraft()` clears an unreadable record with no live model required, re-reads to tell "still unreadable" from "replaced with something readable" (`draftUnreadableAfterDiscard`), and publishes the replacement's `draft`/`writeUncertain` fields the same way `restoreDraft` would on a live store (`decodeKeybindingDraftFields`, new on `keybindingsStore.ts`).

## Findings fixed in this piece (all from #1791's round-6 panel)
- **Medium** (`nativePreferenceDrafts.ts:171`): `draftUnreadableAfterDiscard` cleared the notice whenever the discard's own OUTCOME was `"removed"`/`"absent"`, even if the follow-up read found a FRESH unreadable record. It now takes only the follow-up read's own classification - the discard's outcome plays no part in what is stored NOW.
- **Medium** (`NativePreferencesProvider.tsx:177`): a storage failure during the offline discard returned the same `null` documented for "no hub", making a failed discard indistinguishable from an action that never ran. Returns a distinct `"storageUnavailable"` outcome instead.
- **New** (surfaced during this piece, not in the original panel): the offline probe retained a PREVIOUS hub's `draftUnreadable` flag when a NEW hub's read failed. Scoped by a `probedHubId` ref so a failure right after a hub switch resets to `false` rather than showing the old hub's classification under the new hub's name.
- **Low**: `setBound`'s offline-discard update published only `draftUnreadable`/`storageUnavailable`/`error`, leaving `draft`/`writeUncertain` stale when the discard's re-read found a readable replacement. Now decodes and publishes both via `decodeKeybindingDraftFields`.

`offlineStorageUnavailable` itself is still set but not yet consumed by a screen - that is p6c's own finding (the Low restated against `KeybindingPreferencesScreen.tsx`).

## Gates
- `npx vitest run` (mobile-native, full suite): 833 passed
- `npx vitest run appwire-client/typescript` (from cmd/evener-hub/frontend): 1993 passed
- `npm run typecheck` (cmd/evener-hub/frontend) and `npm run check` (mobile-native): clean
- `npx biome ci ../../../appwire-client/typescript` and `npm run lint` (cmd/evener-hub/frontend): clean
- `make lint-package-imports`: PASS
- `make test-api-package`: qualified (index.ts gained one named export, `decodeKeybindingDraftFields`; no module added/moved)

## Falsification
`draftUnreadableAfterDiscard`'s corrected logic: reproduced the original panel's exact scenario (an "unreadable" follow-up read) as a test, confirmed it fails against a reverted (return-false) implementation, restored.

## Residual (flagged, not fixed here)
`NativePreferencesProvider.tsx` has no test file of its own (true before this change too - the original ~130-line diff that added this feature had none either). The wiring in this piece is exercised only through its downstream screen (p6c) and indirectly through the pure functions it delegates every decision to, all of which ARE unit-tested (`draftUnreadableAfterDiscard`, `clearsErrorAfterOfflineDiscard`, `decodeKeybindingDraftFields`, `readDraftOutcome`, `matchesStoredBytes`). A React Testing Library harness for this provider would be a reasonable follow-up but is out of scope for this stack.

## Non-test line count
`git diff a24e7c59d...HEAD --stat` (this piece's own diff): 209 non-test lines across `index.ts`, `keybindingsStore.ts`, `NativePreferencesProvider.tsx`, `nativePreferenceDrafts.ts`. Above the 80-150 target (the four findings above added scope beyond the base wiring); under the 400 hard ceiling.

title: D6 p6c: keybindings screen offline-recovery UI (closes p6 decomposition)
body:
Stacked on #1902 (p6b); diff against main includes it, #1900 (p6a), and #1808 until they merge. Last of three pieces #1791 (p6) is decomposed into.

## What this piece delivers
`KeybindingPreferencesScreen.tsx` gets the "Discard unreadable draft" action p6a/p6b delivered the store and provider halves of, with the three round-6/round-7 panel findings against it fixed from the start:

- `offlineAwareDraftUnreadable` prefers `preferences.offlineDraftUnreadable` over the live domain snapshot's `draftUnreadable` whenever this screen is disconnected: `domain` is guaranteed stale the moment the connection drops (no live read has happened since), so a record that becomes corrupt - or is fixed - while offline was invisible to it before this fix.
- `unreadableDraftDiscardDisabled` never gates the offline discard action on `domain.saving`/`writeUncertain`: those describe an in-flight or unresolved HUB write, meaningful only on the connected live-store path, and gating the store-free path on a stale one left over from before disconnecting made the one recovery this state allows impossible to reach.
- `offlineStorageErrorMessage` renders `preferences.offlineStorageUnavailable` through the existing `ErrorMessage`, closing the Low that it was tracked but never consumed.

## A gap this piece had to close to wire the above
`nativePreferences.ts`'s `PreferenceState<T>` never declared `draftUnreadable` (default `false`, always `false` for `transcriptMobile`), and `keybindingsDomain()` never bridged `state.draftUnreadable` into its projection - p6a introduced the field on the store and p6b's provider already *wrote* it into the snapshot via `setBound`, but nothing declared it on the shared type, so no code could safely *read* it via `domain.draftUnreadable` (a real gap, not yet a visible bug: no reader existed until this screen tried). Fixed here since it's a small, necessary bridge and this is where the need surfaced.

## Findings fixed in this piece
- **#1791 round-6 Medium / round-7 restated**: the screen made `domain.draftUnreadable` authoritative whenever any snapshot existed, ignoring the independently-computed `offlineDraftUnreadable` - fixed via `offlineAwareDraftUnreadable`.
- **New from p7's (#1792) round-6 panel**: the discard action was also disabled by stale `domain.writeUncertain` while disconnected - fixed via `unreadableDraftDiscardDisabled`.
- **#1791 round-6/round-7 Low**: `offlineStorageUnavailable` tracked but never consumed - fixed via `offlineStorageErrorMessage`.

## Testability
Both new decision functions live in `keybindingOfflineRecovery.ts`, a plain module with no `react-native` import: the screen itself pulls in `react-native` (Flow-syntax source vitest cannot parse), so a test file importing the screen module directly fails to load with a parse error - this is what makes the logic unit-testable at all. `KeybindingPreferencesScreen.tsx`'s own JSX wiring is untested (true before this change too, and unavoidable without a React Testing Library harness this package does not have) - flagged as a residual alongside `NativePreferencesProvider.tsx`'s (p6b).

## Gates
- `npx vitest run` (mobile-native, full suite): 840 passed
- `npx vitest run appwire-client/typescript` (from cmd/evener-hub/frontend): 1993 passed (unaffected; this piece touches mobile-native only)
- `npm run check` (mobile-native) and `npm run typecheck` (cmd/evener-hub/frontend): clean
- biome/lint: unaffected (no appwire-client/typescript or frontend files touched)

## Falsification
- `offlineAwareDraftUnreadable`: reverted to the old domain-first behavior, confirmed the disconnected-preference test fails exactly as the panel described, restored.
- `keybindingRecovery.test.ts`'s strengthened `draftUnreadable: true` assertion: reverted the `keybindingsDomain()` bridging line, confirmed the test fails, restored.

## Non-test line count
`git diff 4c51a14cb...HEAD --stat` (this piece's own diff): 119 non-test lines across `KeybindingPreferencesScreen.tsx`, `keybindingOfflineRecovery.ts`, `nativePreferences.ts`. Within the 80-150 target.

title: D6 piece 7: a keybindings draft carries its own ready generation
body:
## D6 piece 7: a keybindings draft carries its own ready generation

Plan item 7 of the D6 decomposition (`.superpowers/sdd/2026-09-12-mobile-landing-queue-cont/d6-split-plan.md`): "A draft's generation is stamped by its first authoritative payload." Stacks on #1791 (p6).

### Mechanism (adapted from #1549's `10eba05a2`/`dc381b3f5`/`351dc2c6e`)
- `KeybindingsDraft` (local type, distinct from the wire-shaped `KeybindingsOverrides` also used for confirmed hub state and this store's write-path return values): `{ version: 1; revision: number; rules: KeybindingsRule[]; generation: number | null }`.
- `currentGeneration()` helper: `fence.generation >= 0 ? fence.generation : null`.
- `staleDraft`'s third param (`currentGeneration: number`, i.e. `fence.generation`): a non-null generation mismatch is stale regardless of revision, since hub revision numbering restarts on a hub replacement (reconnect to a different hub, or the same hub after a restart) and a coincidentally-identical revision must not read as current.
- Every draft construction site (`restoreDraft`, `editDraft`, `saveDraft`, `rebaseDraft`) stamps `generation: currentGeneration()`.
- `applyHubOverrides` stamps a `generation: null` draft with the live generation as part of accepting the first authoritative payload after it, before judging staleness for that same payload - closing the case where a draft restored before any generation began (a store built synchronously, before the host connects) never gets its generation check activated. Guarded on `fence.generation >= 0` (no call site here reaches this before `beginReadyGeneration` wires the fence, but kept the same shape defensively rather than relying on that staying true).

### Oracle tests
- `a draft restored before any generation began is stamped by the first authoritative payload, so a later hub replacement at the same revision is caught`
- `a draft is flagged stale across a generation change even when the new generation happens to report the same revision`
- Restored `generation: 1` (or `generation: null` for the pre-ready-restore case) to every existing draft-equality assertion the new field now touches (7 sites, not just the 2 the brief named - measured via a full test run after adding the field: `git diff` shows the affected lines).
- Added `draftConflictAfterSettle` to the settle-scenarios table (`saveDraft's post-reply sequence`): a settle that crosses a ready-generation boundary (fenced out by the generation ending, or by support dropping and returning - both begin a new generation) never trusts the draft's revision against it, even though the checkpoint itself settled cleanly.

### Falsification
Reverted only `keybindingsStore.ts` to #1791's head and re-ran `keybindingsStore.test.ts`: 10 failures (the two new tests plus 8 assertions expecting `generation`/`draftConflictAfterSettle` behavior the reverted file doesn't have). Restored with `git apply`; `git status` clean before committing.

## Gates
- `npx vitest run keybindingsStore.test.ts draftCheckpointPort.test.ts` (appwire-client/typescript): 84 passed
- `npx vitest run` (mobile-native, full suite): 797 passed, 83 files
- `npm run typecheck` (cmd/evener-hub/frontend): clean
- `npm run check` (mobile-native): clean
- `npx biome ci ../../../appwire-client/typescript` and `npm run lint` (cmd/evener-hub/frontend): clean
- `make lint-package-imports`: PASS
- `make test-api-package`: qualified (no index.ts/tsconfig.build.json touch, so the falsification wasn't required, but ran it anyway since a new exported interface was added; passes)

title: D6 piece 8: settings-hub generation core (fence/notification wiring, retirePayload)
body:
## D6 piece 8, part 1: fence/notification wiring + payload retirement core

Stacked on #1792 (p7), base main per the queue's serial-merge convention - this PR's own commits are the last one (`git diff -M --stat origin/claude/sdk-d6-p7-draft-generation-stamp...HEAD` below); the rest is p3-p7, already reviewed on their own PRs (#1808, #1791, #1792).

Oracle: PR #1549 @dfde92160's transcriptDisplayStore.ts (a second store not yet built, kept open only as a design check).

### Scope decision - deviates from the plan's literal framing

The predecessor's state note said the generic core should own "fence/notification wiring, retirePayload and the payload-landed bookkeeping (revision/loaded/conflict/appliedSerial)". I read the oracle's actual transcriptDisplayStore.ts (not just the plan text) before writing code, per BRIEF-COMMON's "measure before accepting a review finding/design note" rule, and found:

- `beginReadyGeneration`/`endReadyGeneration` (fence-begin/end + notification wire/unwire) **is** byte-identical between keybindingsStore.ts and the oracle. Extracted as `createSettingsHubGeneration`.
- The in-flight-flags half of `retirePayload` (`loaded`/`saving`/`hubLoading`/`writeUncertain`) **is** identical too (the oracle's version just skips a `revision: 0` reset it has nowhere to apply). Extracted as `retireSettingsHubPayload`.
- The lost-hub write settle (`settleLostHubWrite`/`whyFenced`+`settleUnsettleableWrite` in the oracle) **is** identical. Extracted as `settleUnsettleableWrite`.
- `revision`/`appliedSerial`/`conflict` do **NOT** generalize: `TranscriptDisplayStoreFields` in the oracle has no top-level `revision`, no `appliedSerial` at all, and no `conflict` field - its confirmed defaults are a per-layout map (`hub: Record<ViewportClass, HubTranscriptDisplayDefault>`), each layout carrying its own revision inside the map. Forcing these three into a generic core now would be inventing a shape the oracle contradicts. I left them store-owned.
- `setSupport` stays store-owned per the predecessor's explicit warning - confirmed correct: the oracle's `unsupported` branch has no reconciler un-apply/rollback at all (a display-defaults store has nothing to un-apply), while keybindingsStore.ts's does.

This is "part 1" of the plan's ~510-line estimate in the narrower, verified sense: the three primitives that do generalize, extracted now; the payload-shaped bookkeeping is flagged here for whoever builds piece 10 (transcriptDisplayStore.ts itself) to settle with real code on both sides, not guessed at from the plan's abstract framing.

### Changes
- New `appwire-client/typescript/settingsHubGeneration.ts`: `retireSettingsHubPayload`, `settleUnsettleableWrite`, `createSettingsHubGeneration` (TDD: settingsHubGeneration.test.ts written first, watched fail on the missing module, then implemented).
- `keybindingsStore.ts`: `settleLostHubWrite`, `retirePayload`, `beginReadyGeneration`, `endReadyGeneration` are now thin wrappers composed from the three primitives. No behavior change - the full existing keybindingsStore.test.ts suite (93 tests) passes unchanged.

### Gates (all green)
- `npx vitest run appwire-client/typescript` (full suite): 95 files / 1949 tests
- `npx vitest run` in mobile-native (full suite): 83 files / 797 tests
- `npm run typecheck` in cmd/evener-hub/frontend: clean
- `npm run check` (tsc) in mobile-native: clean
- `npx biome ci ../../../appwire-client/typescript` and `npm run lint` from cmd/evener-hub/frontend: clean
- `make lint-package-imports`: PASS
- `make test-api-package`: qualified (no index.ts change - settingsHubGeneration.ts is not a public export, only imported internally by keybindingsStore.ts, which is already reachable)

New module TDD: settingsHubGeneration.test.ts written against the not-yet-existing module first - `npx vitest run` failed with "Failed to resolve import ./settingsHubGeneration" (12 tests, 0 run); implemented the module; all 12 pass.

title: D6 piece 9: checkpointed draft editor primitives (discard/persist)
body:
## D6 piece 9, part 2: checkpointed draft editor primitives

Stacked on #1841 (piece 8), base main per the queue's serial-merge convention - this PR's own commit is the last one (`git diff -M --stat origin/claude/sdk-d6-p8-settings-hub-generation...HEAD` below); the rest is p3-p8, already reviewed on their own PRs (#1808, #1791, #1792, #1841).

Oracle: PR #1549 @dfde92160's transcriptDisplayStore.ts, same caveat as #1841 - a second store not yet built, kept open only as a design check.

### What generalized, measured against the oracle

- `assertDiscardable`/`assertDraftDiscardable` - byte-identical body between both real stores (`fence.disposed || saving || writeUncertain || (storageUnavailable && !draftUnreadable)`). Fully extracted.
- `discardDraft`/`discardCheckpointedDraft` - the WHOLE body is identical once `restoreDraft` and the message string are parameters: gate, `discardClassified()`, adopt-a-replacement-via-restoreDraft on refusal, the five-field reset on success. Fully extracted.
- `persistDraft`/`persistCheckpointedDraft` - identical mint-id/save/catch shape, **with one real discrepancy** (below).

### What stays store-owned, and why

`editDraft`, `saveDraft`, `rebaseDraft` and the write-settle machinery (`settleWrite`/`settledWrite`) do not generalize cleanly:
- Transcript's draft carries a `layout` field a single-payload store has no equivalent of - one draft field can propose either layout, so "does this edit continue the existing draft" is a per-layout identity check (`existing?.layout === layout`) keybindings never needs. Unifying this needs the same kind of `Payload`-parameterized design piece 8 deferred for `setSupport`, not something to guess at in a `~400`-line extraction PR.
- The oracle predates keybindingsStore.ts's own `settleWrite` consolidation (this queue's D6-1808 simplify round, #1808 commits d13a216d9/162c49532): transcript's `saveDraft` still duplicates the settle-a-write logic inline rather than calling a shared `settleWrite`. It is not a fair comparison for what the CURRENT keybindingsStore.ts should generalize toward - piece 10 should compare against keybindingsStore.ts's post-simplify shape, not against #1549 as shipped, when it decides whether/how `settleWrite` generalizes.

### For whoever builds piece 10 (transcriptDisplayStore.ts) - the revision/appliedSerial/conflict finding from #1841 carries forward here too

#1841 found that `TranscriptDisplayStoreFields` in the oracle has no top-level `revision`, `appliedSerial` or `conflict` at all (a per-layout map instead), so those three don't belong in the generic core. The same is true one level up, for the draft's own identity: keybindings' `KeybindingsDraft.revision` is a single number; transcript's `TranscriptDraft` needs `layout` alongside `revision` to know WHICH per-layout revision it is stale against. Piece 10 should not assume a `Payload`/`Draft` type parameter can be bolted onto `createSettingsHubStore<Payload>` mechanically from these two pieces' primitives - `staleDraft`'s own signature already differs (`staleDraft(draft, confirmedRevision, currentGeneration)` for keybindings vs `staleDraft(draft, hub, currentGeneration)` in the oracle, reading `hub[draft.layout].revision` internally) - it needs a real design pass with both stores' actual code in hand, the same category of decision as `setSupport`.

### A real bug found and fixed along the way

`persistDraft`'s catch only set `storageUnavailable`, never `draftError` - the oracle's sets both. `nativePreferences.ts`'s `keybindingsDomain` projection reads `draftError` first, falling back to a hub-sourced message (`hubErrorMessage`) that says nothing about a local disk error. A user whose keybinding edit failed to persist locally (`editDraft`, `saveDraft` or `rebaseDraft` failing at the `persistDraft` step) saw `storageUnavailable: true` with **no error message at all** - `hubErrorMessage` returns `null` for this case (neither `loadError` nor `hubError` describe a draft-port failure).

Fixed by generalizing `persistCheckpointedDraft` to set both fields, matching the oracle. Pinned with a new test in keybindingsStore.test.ts (falsified: failed with `draftError: null` against the pre-fix code, paste below).

### Changes
- New `appwire-client/typescript/checkpointedDraftEditor.ts`: `assertDraftDiscardable`, `persistCheckpointedDraft`, `discardCheckpointedDraft` (TDD: checkpointedDraftEditor.test.ts written first against the not-yet-existing module, watched fail, then implemented - 11 tests).
- `keybindingsStore.ts`: `assertDiscardable`, `persistDraft`, `discardDraft` are now thin wrappers.
- `keybindingsStore.test.ts`: one new test pinning the draftError fix.

### Gates (all green)
- `npx vitest run appwire-client/typescript` (full suite): 96 files / 1961 tests
- `npx vitest run` in mobile-native (full suite): 83 files / 797 tests
- `npm run typecheck` in cmd/evener-hub/frontend: clean
- `npm run check` (tsc) in mobile-native: clean
- `npx biome ci ../../../appwire-client/typescript` and `npm run lint` from cmd/evener-hub/frontend: clean
- `make lint-package-imports`: PASS
- `make test-api-package`: qualified (no index.ts change)

### Falsification
New module: checkpointedDraftEditor.test.ts against the not-yet-existing module failed with "Failed to resolve import" (11 tests, 0 run); implemented; all 11 pass.
Bug fix: the new keybindingsStore.test.ts test ("editDraft's persistDraft failure marks draftError, not just storageUnavailable") failed against pre-fix persistDraft with `draftError: null` where `"Could not save the shortcut draft locally."` was expected; passes after the fix.

title: D6 piece 10: transcriptDisplayStore hub defaults + direct write
body:
## D6 piece 10: transcriptDisplayStore hub defaults + direct write

Stacked on #1844 (piece 9), base main per the queue's serial-merge convention.

Oracle: PR #1549 @dfde92160's transcriptDisplayStore.ts / transcriptDisplayStore.test.ts, for the read (hub defaults) and write (direct write) path specifically - the checkpointed draft editor half is out of scope (D6 piece 12).

### Size: over the ~400 non-test-line guideline, with a specific reason

`git diff --stat` for this PR's own commit: readyGenerationFence.ts +19, transcriptDisplayStore.ts +517 (345 code lines, 127 comment lines, 45 blank - counted with an awk pass, not just eyeballed). This is a genuinely new store, not an extraction like pieces 8/9, so it doesn't shrink the way those did. I kept the oracle's comment density (matching this codebase's established style of explaining WHY, not just WHAT) rather than trim it to hit the number. If you'd rather I cut this into two PRs after the fact (read path / write path), say so - I didn't split it because the plan's own item 10 names them as one unit ("hub defaults + the direct write") and splitting them now would require stubbing one half against the other with no real boundary to justify the seam.

### What's adopted directly from pieces 8/9 - zero re-derivation

- `createSettingsHubGeneration` (piece 8) for `beginReadyGeneration`/`endReadyGeneration` and the notification wiring.
- `retireSettingsHubPayload` (piece 8) for the in-flight-flags reset in `retirePayload`; the per-layout `patchTokens` reset (transcript-specific bookkeeping the shared fence knows nothing about) is layered on top by claiming a fresh `fence.claimWrite()` per layout before delegating, rather than trying to read `fence.writeToken` after the shared primitive's own internal `supersede()` - order-independent and correct either way a caller sequences it.
- `settleUnsettleableWrite` (piece 8) is **not used** here: I initially imported it, then found it (via `whyFenced`) is only ever called from the oracle's `saveDraft` (piece 12), never from `patchHubDefault` or `refreshFor`. Removed the unused import before pushing.
- Piece 9's `assertDraftDiscardable`/`persistCheckpointedDraft`/`discardCheckpointedDraft` are **not used** here either - discard/persist are checkpointed-editor-only concerns, entirely out of piece 10's scope.

### A real gap found in the shared fence, fixed here (additive, keybindings untouched)

The oracle's `readyGenerationFence.ts` (shipped inside #1549) has two members ours doesn't: `awaitingFirstPayload` / `firstPayloadApplied()`. keybindings' `retirePayload` resets `revision: 0` on every generation end, so nothing is ever "previous" going into a new generation and a hub restart's lower revision is never wrongly compared. Transcript's `hub` is deliberately **retained** across a transient disconnect (the effective configuration must not flap - `hub`'s own field doc says so), so its stale-guard needs an explicit "this generation has confirmed nothing yet, so the next payload is authoritative at any revision" escape hatch keybindings never needed. Added both members to the shared `ReadyGenerationFence` interface and implementation, TDD'd in `readyGenerationFence.test.ts` (2 new tests, watched fail with "awaitingFirstPayload is not a function" / `undefined`, then implemented). keybindingsStore.ts never reads or sets either member - confirmed by the full keybindingsStore.test.ts suite (90 tests) passing unchanged.

### Oracle hunks dropped as dead (piece 12's job, not lost - listed for whoever builds it)

- `restoreDraft`, `draftCheckpoint`, `staleDraft`, `invalidDraft`, the `discardStoredDraft` re-export - all draft-port-shaped, no port exists yet.
- `initialState()`'s `draft`/`storageUnavailable`/`draftUnreadable`/`draftConflict`/`draftError` fields and the `TranscriptDisplayStoreDeps.drafts` dependency.
- `applyHubDefault`'s draft-generation-stamping block (the `const draft = state.draft !== null && ... ? {...} : state.draft` dance) and its `draftConflict: staleDraft(draft, hub, fence.generation)` field - piece 10's `applyHubDefault` only publishes `hub`/preview-clearing/`extra`.
- `refreshFor`'s `settledWrite(...)` spread into the mobile layout's `extra` - nothing to settle without a checkpoint.
- `patchHubDefault`'s gate clause `|| state.saving || state.writeUncertain` (the checkpointed editor's sibling gate) - the two fields are declared (piece 8's primitive requires them) but nothing sets them yet, so checking them now would be permanently-dead code; piece 12 adds the clause when it adds `saveDraft`.
- `editDraft`/`saveDraft`/`discardDraft`/`rebaseDraft`/`settledWrite`/`whyFenced`/`claimLayoutWrite`-adjacent draft bookkeeping - all piece 12.
- Test-side: the oracle's `"the checkpointed draft editor"` describe block (600 lines) and the checkpoint-coupled direct-write tests within `"the direct write"` (a later checkpointed write superseding an earlier direct write's reply; a direct write refused while a checkpointed write owns the layer; an older save's late reply; rejections/supersession clearing `saving`) - all call `saveDraft`/`rebaseDraft`, which don't exist yet. The `"a retired payload fences..."` matrix test is ported with its `saveDraft` path and the `editDraft` throw-assertion dropped (2 paths x 4 reset sites instead of 3x4).
- `transcriptDisplayStore.ts` is **not yet exported from index.ts** and **not yet in tsconfig.build.json's `files` list** - nothing in the package imports it, so `tsc -p tsconfig.build.json` never compiles it (verified: ran it directly, zero errors, confirming it's simply not part of the build graph yet, not silently broken). Whichever piece wires the first real consumer (11 or 12) should add both.

- `npx vitest run appwire-client/typescript` (full suite): 97 files / 2002 tests
- `npx vitest run` in mobile-native (full suite): 83 files / 797 tests
- `npm run typecheck` in cmd/evener-hub/frontend: clean
- `npm run check` (tsc) in mobile-native: clean
- `npx biome ci ../../../appwire-client/typescript` and `npm run lint` from cmd/evener-hub/frontend: clean
- `make lint-package-imports`: PASS
- `make test-api-package`: qualified (doesn't touch this file - see above)

### Falsification
readyGenerationFence: the two new tests failed against the pre-fix fence (`expected undefined to be true`, `firstPayloadApplied is not a function`); pass after the fence extension.
transcriptDisplayStore.test.ts: failed on module resolution against the not-yet-existing file (0 tests run); all 39 adapted oracle tests passed on the first run once implemented - no debugging round needed, which I read as the pre-write measurement (reading the oracle's actual patchHubDefault/applyHubDefault/refreshFor bodies before writing anything) having paid off rather than as nothing having been exercised: the 39 tests cover the stale-guard, the per-layout preview/contradiction rules, the conflict/malformed/fenced-reply paths and the awaitingFirstPayload cases directly.

title: agent: restore derives the pending ask from the boundary the live path uses
body:
## Summary
Second of three tiny PRs decomposing #1806. Piece 2 of 3.

Stacked on #1905 (piece 1: the live-side steer/carrier gating); diff against
main includes it until it merges.

- `turnResolvesAskBoundary` (`agent/session_tools_ask.go`) factors the
  decisive-turn table `deriveRestoredState`/`deriveRestoredAskPending` both
  need (`TurnUserInput`, a resolving `TurnSteering`, a `TurnFailure` tagged
  `SteeringCarrier`) once, so the two backward scans can't independently
  disagree with each other or with the live path piece 1 added.
- `steeringOriginBoundary` replaces `escapeHistoryWithSessionProvenance`'s
  own inline clamp and is now shared with the two restore functions: a
  forked child's inherited prefix is decided with `nil` steering-journal
  provenance regardless of the child's own journal, so a reused
  `ClientMutationID` in the child's journal can never reclassify a turn the
  parent wrote. A kindless legacy steering turn (persisted before
  `SteeringKind` was stamped) still reads its provenance from the
  client-mutation journal instead of defaulting to "answers".
- Fixes the open Medium from round 6 of #1806's review
  (`session_tools_ask.go:539-542`): `deriveRestoredAskPending`'s "generic
  completion is decisive" branches assumed the round's entry already
  cleared `askPending` live — true for a genuine user reply, false for a
  non-resolving human-note carrier. `roundEntryResolvesAskBoundary` walks
  back to the round's entry turn and asks the same question about it, so a
  generic completion inside a non-resolving carrier's round no longer stops
  the scan before it reaches the still-pending ask.

## Test plan
- `go test -count=1 -run 'TestAskUser|TestRestored|TestInherited|TestHistoryCopy|TestRebuilt' ./agent/` — green, plain, `-race` (on the restore-dependent subset), and `-tags evenerfuzz`.
- `$(go env GOROOT)/bin/gofmt -l`, `go vet ./...`, `go vet -tags evenerfuzz ./...`, `GOOS=windows go vet -tags evenerfuzz ./...`, `golangci-lint run ./...` — all clean.

- The two negative "does not resolve" tests carried over from piece 1
  (`TestAskUser_RestoreDoesNotResolveAcrossAFailedHumanNoteCarrierAppend`,
  `TestAskUser_RecordFailedSteeringSelectionDoesNotTagAHumanNoteClaim`) pass
  under piece 1 alone by accident (the old restore scan ignores
  `TurnFailure` entirely) and only really exercise the interaction once this
  piece's tag-reading exists. Falsified that interaction directly:
  temporarily made piece 1's `SteeringCarrier` tag unconditional (both
  gating call sites) with this piece's restore-reading left intact — both
  tests failed with `restored askPending = [], want 1 question`; restored,

title: feat(mobile): screens survive a connection flap behind a banner (D28 D2)
body:
Stacked on #1912 (the hubConnection follow-ups PR): this branch is built on
top of it because this PR also touches `hubConnection.ts` (adding `fatal`).
The diff below therefore includes #1912's commit until that one merges;
only this PR's own commit (`d86b50bf4`) needs reviewing here.

Per Jesse's ruling 7 (2026-09-18, #1595): screens survive a connection flap
behind a banner instead of the full-screen Reconnect wall. Closes #1595.

## Measurement

- The wall: `PluginsScreen.tsx`, `HubSettingsScreen.tsx` and
  `ProvidersScreen.tsx` all had the same shape - `if (!client || state !==
  "ready") return <View>...Reconnect...</View>` (or the ternary
  equivalent) - unmounting the ready-only child (and its store, scroll
  position, selection) on ANY non-ready transition, including a passive
  auto-reconnect where the underlying `AppwireClient` never even changes
  identity.
- The web equivalent (`cmd/evener-hub/frontend/src/shell/ConnectionBanner.tsx`):
  the workspace always stays mounted; a floating banner appears only for
  `ATTENTION_STATES = {"reconnecting", "closed"}`, after a `delayMs` grace
  window (10s default - "a routine sub-second reconnect never surfaces, a
  genuinely stuck connection tells the user promptly"). That's what "brief
  flap" means on the web: immediate banner-eligibility, delayed reveal - not
  something D2 needed to reproduce (mobile's own reconnect backoff, and this
  PR's own everReady/fatal gating, already keep a routine blip silent-ish
  behind a banner rather than a wall; a reveal-delay timer is a separate,
  optional polish this PR does not add).
- `#1595`'s own body already named the fix in two halves: "screens stay
  mounted... (then the native wiring of connectionChanged becomes the
  SECOND HALF of that change)". This PR is the first half only. Filed the
  second half as prime-radiant-inc/evener#1914 (PluginsScreen's store has no
  push-notification reconnect recovery - `connectionChanged` is never
  called - though a passive flap alone doesn't need it, since `client`'s
  identity is stable through one; only a missed hub-side change during the
  blip would be stale, which #1914 covers).

## Design

`connectionDisplay(state, everReady, fatal)` (`mobile-native/src/connectionDisplay.ts`,
pure, react-native-free per #1908's constraint):
- `"none"` once `state === "ready"`.
- `"wall"` when the screen has never shown anything yet (`!everReady`), or
  the close is fatal (a protocol mismatch a retry can never fix).
- `"banner"` for every other non-ready state, once something has already
  been shown - the flap the screen now survives.

`useConnectionDisplay(state, fatal)` wraps it with an `everReady` ref
(mutated during render, the same pattern `ForkScreen.tsx`'s `owner.current`
already uses).

`fatal` is new on `HubConnection`/`Connection` (`hubConnection.ts`,
`ConnectionProvider.tsx`): true only for a protocol close, computed
alongside the existing error-message classification, reset on every fresh
attempt.

`ConnectionStatus` (the existing status-row banner `screens.tsx` already
used for the Sessions/Conversation lists - name/state text + a conditional
Reconnect action + `ErrorMessage`) is reused rather than building a new
banner. It had to move out of `screens.tsx` into its own file first:
`screens.tsx` pulls in `@react-navigation/elements` (among a large import
graph), which fails to load under vitest (a `.png` asset import) - a VALUE
import of `ConnectionStatus` from a test-reached module broke
`ProvidersScreen.test.tsx` until the move (measured: reproduced the
failure, fixed by extraction, confirmed green).

Plugins/HubSettings additionally track the last non-null client in a ref:
`client` stays set through a passive flap (hubConnection.ts's own
generation guard), but a manual retry's token-refetch window does clear it
briefly, and the last-known-client fallback keeps the child mounted through
that gap too rather than dropping to the wall for a moment the banner
already covers. `ProvidersScreen` needs no such fallback -
`useCredentialStore()` already survives a flap on its own
(`connectionChanged` rebinds it, `credentialStore.ts`), and `<Providers>`
takes only `store`, never `client`, directly.

## Auto-refresh (native rule: never a manual "refresh to see the latest" affordance)

- `ProvidersScreen`: already correct via `connectionChanged`'s reconnect
  recovery (pre-existing, unaffected by this PR).
- `HubSettingsScreen`: `createHubOverviewStore` has no push notification by
  design (its own module doc: "no push-driven invalidation... callers
  decide when to fetch()/refresh()") and already offers pull-to-refresh
  (`RefreshControl`) - a standard native idiom, not the banned affordance.
  Nothing to add.
- `PluginsScreen`: a passive flap never changes `client` identity, so
  nothing was stale to begin with for that case. A missed hub-side plugin
  change during a flap this screen was disconnected for is a real,
  pre-existing gap (confirmed: `connectionChanged` was never called) -
  filed as #1914 rather than bundled here, matching #1595's own two-halves
  framing.

## Tests (mobile-native has no RTL harness - #1908)

- `connectionDisplay.test.ts`: the pure function's 4 branches, plus
  `useConnectionDisplay` hook tests for the three named scenarios - "ready
  -> reconnecting keeps mounted + banner", "reconnecting -> ready removes
  the banner", "fatal shows the wall even after having been ready".
- `hubConnection.test.tsx`: `fatal` reports true only for a protocol close,
  clears on `"ready"` and on a fresh attempt's own generation.
- `ProvidersScreen.test.tsx` (extends the one existing real-mount screen
  test - `PluginsScreen`/`HubSettingsScreen` have no test file to extend,
  a pre-existing gap #1908 already tracks): the same three scenarios driven
  through the REAL mounted screen via `tree.update` + the mocked
  `useConnection` - the list's rendered rows stay present through
  `reconnecting`, the banner text appears and disappears with `state`, and
  a fatal close replaces the list with the wall.

## Falsification

- `connectionDisplay.ts` moved aside: `connectionDisplay.test.ts` failed on
  the missing module; restored, green.
- `ProvidersScreen.tsx` reverted to its pre-PR content: the new "ready ->
  reconnecting keeps ... mounted" test failed (list content gone, replaced
  by the wall) exactly as measured; restored, green; `git status --short`
  showed only the intended files throughout.

## Gates

- `npx vitest run` (mobile-native): 86 files / 821 tests passed
- `npm run check` (mobile-native, tsc): clean
- `make lint-package-imports`: PASS (no `appwire-client` files touched)

## Diff (includes #1912's commit until it merges - see the stacking note above)

```
$(git diff -M --stat origin/main...HEAD)
```

Closes #1595.

title: feat(native): MutationOutboxStorage write path over expo-sqlite (D25d-1a)
body:
D25d-1, split per the coordinator's ruling since the drafted adapter (302 non-test lines for all 13 port methods) exceeded the ~150 target: 1a is the write path (enqueueIntent, markAttempted, markUnknown, settleReceipt, settleApplied, transferToRecovery), 1b (stacked on this, base main, opened separately) adds the read path (getOutbox, getOptimistic, listOptimistic, getRecovery, nextDispatchable, listTargetRefs, restoreProvenAbsent) to the same class.

## What this implements

The phone's implementation of the package's `MutationOutboxStorage` port (`appwire-client/typescript/state/mutation/outbox.ts`) over a synchronous SQLite handle - `expo-sqlite`'s `openDatabaseSync` in production, `node:sqlite`'s `DatabaseSync` in tests. This is the same storage `draftRepository.ts` already persists drafts through (three/four tables instead of five, same synchronous-handle-wrapped-in-promises shape).

**No host global named in the package.** The sqlite handle (`MutationOutboxDatabase`, a 4-method port: `execSync`/`runSync`/`getFirstSync`/`getAllSync`) lives entirely in this adapter, in `mobile-native/`, mirroring `draftRepository.ts`'s `DraftDatabase` port convention.

One row shape serves all three tables (outbox/optimistic/recovery): a record's current table IS its state, so no separate state machine duplicates what table membership already says.

## Test harness (measured, not assumed)

`draftRepository.test.ts` already runs the native draft storage against `node:sqlite`'s `DatabaseSync`, not `expo-sqlite` (unavailable outside a device/simulator) and not a mock - a real, if different, SQLite engine over the same synchronous port shape. This PR's tests do the same. `node:sqlite` is a Node built-in (stable in this repo's Node v26), not an npm dependency - no `npm ci` needed, nothing missing from `node_modules`.

## Oracle

`cmd/evener-hub/frontend/src/stores/mutationOutbox.test.ts`'s `describe("MutationOutboxIndexedDB", ...)` block (lines 67-556) is the reference. Each of this PR's 10 tests mirrors one of its assertions, cited by name in a comment at the call site:
- "reload restores the complete persisted intent" (`:105`) -> `enqueueIntent persists a submitting record with the full intent`
- "concurrent tabs allocate one gap-free per-target sequence" (`:176`) -> `intentSequence is gap-free and per target ref`
- "a pending receipt atomically hands input display from transport outbox to durable optimistic state" (`:235`) -> `settleReceipt moves a pending, input-carrying record into the optimistic table`
- "a pending receipt settles a receipt-only control without creating optimistic display" (`:280`) -> `settleReceipt drops a receipt-only control with no optimistic input to carry`
- "applied settlement dominates unknown in either response order..." (`:193`) -> `settleApplied removes a record from whichever table currently holds it`
- "a rejection carries its reason into recovery" (`:221`) -> `transferToRecovery moves a record out of the outbox and carries the daemon's reason`

Not ported: the web's Blob/attachment-bytes handling, cross-tab client identity (`originClientId` is read through an injected `getOwnClientId` port here, wired in D25d-2), and shared-notes recovery-superseding (`#discardSupersededNoteRecovery` in the web's class) - none of which the `MutationOutboxStorage` port itself declares. Flagging the last one as a residual: if native's queue ever needs the same shared-notes recovery behavior, that's separate work, not part of this port.

Since the read methods (`getOutbox` etc.) don't exist yet in this PR, tests verify each write's effect against the raw SQLite row rather than through a read method - `rawRow(table, id)` queries the underlying `node:sqlite` handle directly.

## Falsification

Moved `mutationOutboxStorage.ts` out of the tree: the test file failed with `Cannot find module './mutationOutboxStorage'`. Restored; `git status --short` showed only the two intended files.

## Gates

- `npx vitest run src/mutationOutboxStorage.test.ts`: **10 passed (10)**.
- `npm run check` (mobile-native tsc): clean.
- `make lint-package-imports`: PASS.
- Not run: biome/lint - `mobile-native/` has no biome config (memory: never run biome over `mobile/` or `mobile-native/`), confirmed by `package.json` having no lint/format script. Matched the directory's own style (tabs, via `perl` conversion checked against `draftRepository.ts`'s indentation).

## Diff stat

```
$(git diff -M --stat origin/main...HEAD)
```

254 non-test lines (`mutationOutboxStorage.ts`) - over the ~150 target even after the split, because the schema, row (de)serialization and `insert`/`get`/`delete` helpers all have to exist somewhere before either half can do anything, and 1a is where they land. 1b should be much smaller (it only adds thin read methods reusing this plumbing).

## Next

D25d-1b (read path, stacked on this) opens separately, base main, titled to note it stacks on this PR.

title: fix(mobile): the conversation keeps its turns and wire cursor coherent across paging and rehydrate
body:
Decomposed out of #1885 after five review rounds (Jesse's "five review rounds means decompose" rule). This PR is the state-layer mechanism only: `mobile/src/state/conversation.ts` and `mobile/src/services/conversation.ts`'s turn plumbing. #1885's footer half is B3a, stacked on this PR.

## What this closes

The store's own top-level `olderCursor` (a UI-only, intentionally capped "is there another page to fetch" signal, F8) and the conversation's own `ThreadModel.olderCursor` (the wire truth `sessionTokens` reads) are two different values that #1885's review kept finding collapsed into one at different sites, across five rounds:

- **loadOlder** derives `conversation.olderCursor` from the wire's own `nextCursor`, never the store's capped field (so the item cap stopping the UI's own paging never mislabels a partial sum as a full session).
- **rehydrate** preserves page-loaded turn history across a same-session reread: its own itemLimit-bounded window can't see turns loaded by an earlier `loadOlder`. Turn ownership is tracked separately from item ownership (`pageOwnedTurnIds`, alongside the existing `pageOwnedIds`), so a page whose display rows were all deduped or evicted still keeps its turns for the merge.
- **rehydrate's cursor** carries the prior conversation's own wire cursor only when the merge actually contributed a turn beyond the fresh read's own window - not whenever page history merely exists somewhere in the session's lifetime.
- **Both merges** (loadOlder's and rehydrate's) go through the package's own `mergeOlderItemPage` (`turnsMatch`/`mergePageTurn`) instead of an id-only filter: `thread/turns/list` is itself item-paginated, so a turn can be split into fragments across a page boundary, or two turns can be logically the same but carry different ids. The service now exposes the wire `ThreadTurnsListResponse` (`turnsPage`) from both `loadOlder` and `readProjection` so the store folds it through the package's real, identity-aware merge - never a second, hand-rolled one.

## Per-state table (a session with no thread-level cumulative usage, so sessionTokens is always summing turns)

| state | store cursor | conversation cursor | turns | scope |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| initial (open) | `null` (F8's live path establishes it separately) | `"cursor-1"` (from the hydrated model) | `[t2]` | `loaded` |
| loadOlder (wire has more) | `"cursor-2"` | `"cursor-2"` (= wire `nextCursor`) | `[t1, t2]` | `loaded` |
| cap hit (wire still has more) | `null` (F8 stops paging honestly) | `"more"` (unaffected by the cap) | `[t1, t2]` | `loaded` |
| rehydrate, page history kept, contributes beyond the fresh window | unchanged | prior conversation's own wire cursor | merged (identity-aware) | `loaded` |
| rehydrate, page history exists but the fresh window already covers it | unchanged | fresh read's own | fresh reread's own | per fresh read |
| rehydrate, no page history | fresh read's own | fresh read's own | fresh reread's own | per fresh read |

A test per row lives in `mobile/src/state/conversation.test.ts`'s two `describe` blocks ("D18 B3 round 5" and "D18 B3 round 6").

## Failing-first tests (watched fail against `origin/main`, pass with the fix)

- `merges the older page's turns into conversation.turns and advances conversation.olderCursor`
- `keeps conversation.olderCursor at the wire's cursor even when the item cap stops paging`
- `rehydrate preserves the older turns loaded via loadOlder`
- `cap hit then rehydrate: conversation.olderCursor stays the wire truth, not the store's capped null`
- `evicted/filtered page: a turn survives a rehydrate even when none of that page's items did`
- `a turn split across a page boundary keeps its usage instead of being dropped by an id-only filter`
- `rehydrate with page history but a fully-covering fresh window: scope follows the fresh read, not a stale accumulated cursor`
- `returns the older page's wire turns alongside items`

## Falsification

Reverted `mobile/src/services/conversation.ts` and `mobile/src/state/conversation.ts` alone to `origin/main`, ran `mobile/src/state/conversation.test.ts` and `mobile/src/services/conversation.test.ts`: 8 failed exactly as above. Restored from the saved diff; `git status --short` showed only the 4 intended files.

## Gates

- `npx vitest run --root .. --config mobile-native/vitest.config.mts mobile/src/state/conversation.test.ts mobile/src/services/conversation.test.ts`: 485 passed.
- Full `mobile-native` suite (`npx vitest run`): 798 real tests pass (3 pre-existing `react-test-renderer`-missing file-load failures, present on `origin/main` before this PR too).
- Shared `mobile/src` suite (`npm run test:shared`): 801 pass.
- `npm run check` (tsc, mobile-native): same 4 pre-existing errors as `origin/main`.
- No `appwire-client/typescript` or `cmd/evener-hub/frontend` files touched.

## Diff

```
$(git diff -M --stat origin/main...HEAD)
```
84 non-test lines in `mobile/src/state/conversation.ts` + 18 in `mobile/src/services/conversation.ts` = 102 non-test lines (target 80-150, ~180 ceiling if the merge reuse needed it - it didn't need the extra room).

## What this is

The phone's transcript footer reads the same turn-summed session usage totals the web details panel reads, with the same scope fallback, so both surfaces show the same session figure for a session with no thread-level cumulative usage (a fork child never gets one stamped, per `agent/fork.go`'s `writeForkChild`).

- `accountingFor` derives the footer's token total from the package's `sessionTokens(conversation)` instead of reading `conversation.usage` directly.

- `usageRows` picks the footer's visible rows and gives each its own unit, so a turn-summed "loaded" pair can't leak its label onto an unrelated whole-session cache/total figure.
- A field's Go zero value is treated the same as absent (`cacheReadTokens`/`totalTokens` of `0`), matching `sessionTokens`'s own rule for input/output tokens.
- `tokenUnitLabel` (the `SessionTokens` scope-to-label mapping) is shared, in `appwire-client/typescript/threadUsage.ts` — the web details panel and the native footer render the same `"tokens (loaded turns)"` / `"tokens"` wording from one function. `DetailsPanel.test.tsx` is unchanged and still passes — the rendered string never moved.

title: fix(agent): stop retirement eligibility checks racing the async session namer (#1879)
body:
## Root cause

`launchInitialPromptNamer` / `launchCompactionNamerGated` (`agent/session_namer.go`) start the background session namer in its own goroutine (`s.naming.pending++`, `go func() { defer s.finishSessionNamer(release); ... }()`) and never join it before the triggering turn (`ProcessInput`) returns. While that goroutine is in flight it correctly holds an `"autonomous"` retirement blocker via `s.naming.pending != 0` (`agent/session_retirement_evidence.go:76`).

`assertRetirementEvidenceEligible` is the shared test helper (`agent/session_retirement_evidence_test.go`) that more than a dozen `session_retirement_*_test.go` tests call right after a turn/delegate settles, asserting full eligibility. It never waited for that namer goroutine, so on a loaded CI runner (this issue's "dozens of concurrent CI jobs") the assertion can observe the namer still in flight and fail with exactly the `"settled owner not eligible: {Phase:resident ... Blockers:[{Category:autonomous SessionID:... DelegateID:}] Failure:}, <nil>"` text from every occurrence logged on #1879.

This explains 3 of the 4 named tests (5 of the 6 logged CI occurrences):
- `TestRetirementAttentionArmRetryPending` — via `retirementIdleDelegate` → `retirementSettleDelegate`'s `root.ProcessInput("settle-root-sentinel", ...)`, root's first non-empty turn.
- `TestRetirementSafetyColdJobWatchContent` — same path, on the restored `root2` after a simulated crash/restart.
- `TestRetirementSafetyDetachedLifetime` — root's own first successfully-processed `ProcessInput("launch independent detached process", ...)`.

`TestRetirementTreeSettleDrainsPendingRootAttention` (the 4th named test, 1 of the 6 occurrences) shows the identical blocker shape (`Category:autonomous`, no `DelegateID`) but never calls `ProcessInput` on root before its critical assertion, and its critical check doesn't go through `assertRetirementEvidenceEligible`. I could not reproduce it locally (100 iterations under `GOMAXPROCS=2` + heavy CPU contention, 0 failures) or pin its exact mechanism in the time budgeted. Filed as a separate note on #1879 rather than folded into this fix — see issue comment.

## Fix

Wait on the session's existing `sendersWG` (the same primitive `TestRetirementAutonomousNamingOverlap` already uses for this exact purpose) inside `assertRetirementEvidenceEligible`, before reading evidence. This closes the race for every one of its ~15+ callers at once, rather than patching call sites individually. Test-only change, 0 non-test lines.

Added `TestRetirementEvidenceEligibleAwaitsInFlightNamer`: forces the exact interleaving via the existing `namerClient` test hook (a held channel, no sleeps/wall-clock literals) so the namer is provably still in flight at the assertion.

## Reproduction numbers

- Deterministic forced-interleaving probe (new test): **fails 5/5** before the fix, **passes 20/20** after it.
- Statistical reproduction attempts (did not reproduce naturally — confirms this is a narrow, load-dependent window, consistent with 6 hits across "dozens of concurrent" CI jobs in one day vs. thousands of local runs):

title: fix(native): a collision-resistant, memoized identity for a question set
body:
Piece E of the #1580 decomposition plan (see the [decomposition plan comment](https://github.com/prime-radiant-inc/evener/pull/1580#issuecomment-5723104182)). **Stacked on #1737 (piece C)** — targets `main`, will be refreshed onto `main` after C lands.

## Summary
- Cut from #1580 (`53bb2b6ca`, which already includes the original round-20 `questionsIdentity` fix): `questionAnswers.ts`, `QuestionSheet.tsx`, `screens.tsx`.
- Fixes both of today's new Mediums, found by RoboRev reviewing that round-20 fix itself:
  1. **Collision**: `questionsIdentity` hashed a *bounded* (truncated) copy of each question's canonical fields, so two questions sharing a prefix past the display bound (`MAX_ITEM_BYTES`) collided on the same identity.
  2. **O(payload) per render**: every render/keystroke rehashed the whole payload from scratch, even when the question-array reference (the one `reconcileBatches.ts` hands back unchanged when nothing changed) had not moved.
- Fix: hash the canonical fields directly with `cyrb53` (a fixed-size, collision-resistant, non-cryptographic hash — two 32-bit lanes mixed in one pass, no dependency) instead of truncating first, and memoize by question-array reference in a `WeakMap` so an unaffected render never rehashes at all.

## Test plan
- `npx vitest run --config mobile-native/vitest.config.mts mobile-native/src/questionAnswers.test.ts mobile-native/src/questionBatches.test.ts mobile-native/src/draftRepository.test.ts mobile/src/state/conversation.test.ts mobile/src/conversation/project.test.ts` — 494/494 pass. Two new tests measure the fix directly: a collision test (two oversized questions sharing a `MAX_ITEM_BYTES`-scale prefix now get distinct identities — RED against the pre-fix code) and a memoization test (200 repeated calls with the same array reference stay within 10x a single fresh computation — RED against the pre-fix code, which took >2s for the equivalent case before this test's numbers were dialed down for CI).

title: transcript,agent: the fold names its retained entries by Seq (piece A2 of the #1100 split, closes #1200)
body:
Piece A2 of the #1100 split (rebuilt on the transcript's durable `Entry.Seq` after #1281 was closed). **Closes #1200.**

## The bug (#1200)

After a fold, live history keeps the retained tail verbatim, but a restart resumed only the fold's SUMMARY. `ResumeHistory` anchored on the last CHECKPOINT/SUMMARY marker and discarded every entry before it, while the retained tail's entries sit *before* that marker. The old machinery (`persistedAppendLog` → `rewriteTail`) re-appended only the turns recorded *during* the fold, after the markers — never the preserved recent tail — so the tail vanished on restart.

## The fix

The fold now writes ONE durable `FOLD_RECORD` entry — a manifest naming, by transcript `Seq`, exactly the entries its published history is made of:

- `Layers`: the head marker's Seq (the summary, or the checkpoint when summarization did not run).
- `RetainedSeqs`: the pre-existing turns the fold kept (preserved tail + during-fold merge-back + injected steering), in history order.

The record is written last, after the markers and steering, so everything after it is live post-fold history. On restart, `ResumeHistory` finds the last fold record and rebuilds `[Layers entries] ++ [RetainedSeqs entries] ++ [entries after the record]`, each looked up by Seq. Because `recordTurn` already writes the *persisted* form as the entry and stamps the live turn's Seq to it, naming an entry by Seq yields the identical persisted content the old `rewriteTail` re-appended — without any duplicate entry.

Deleted wholesale: `persistedAppendLog`, `logPairPersistedLocked`, `persistedAppendLogBase`, `rewriteTail` (the fold's `snapAppends` snapshot bookkeeping goes with them).

New/changed:
- `schema.Turn.Seq int` (`json:"-"`, in-memory only): the durable per-line id, stamped at append or seeded from the entry on restore.
- `schema.FoldRecord` + `schema.TurnFoldRecord`; `Turn.Fold *FoldRecord` (`json:"fold_record,omitempty"`).
- `transcript.Writer` `Append`/`AppendDurable`/`AppendSynced` and the session write helpers now return the spent Seq.
- `ResumeHistory`/`resumeHistoryIndexed` reconstruct from the fold record; a pre-A2 transcript (marker, no record) falls back to the legacy last-marker anchor so an in-flight session's first restart after the upgrade does not suddenly replay its long-discarded prefix.
- Fork-provenance in `session_init.go` is decided per turn: `inheritedProvenanceTurns` maps `DivergenceTurn` through each resumed turn's own origin entry (and through the repair insertions), because a fold interleaves provenance — its own head marker, the parent turns it retained, its own tail — which no single boundary index can express. Byte-identical to the old contiguous-window math for the non-fold-record paths.

The `FOLD_RECORD` is never added to `Session.history`: `expandHistory` never sees it, and the reload projector emits no item for it (`default` case), so no projector shape change.

## Old-reader break — option 1, MEASURED (needs Jesse's ruling before merge)

Built under option 1 (no backward-compat machinery). `Turn.Fold` is a new wire field, so `decodeStrictJSON`'s `DisallowUnknownFields` (kata wf7e) makes a transcript that carries a fold record **unreadable to a pre-A2 daemon**. Measured with the exact strict decode against a `schema.Turn` that lacks the field:

```
A2 fold-record entry on the wire:
{"kind":"entry","seq":7,"turn":{"kind":"FOLD_RECORD","message":{"role":"","content":null},"timestamp":"0001-01-01T00:00:00Z","usage":{"input_tokens":0,"output_tokens":0,"total_tokens":0},"fold_record":{"fold_id":"3","layers":[5],"retained_seqs":[2,3,4]}}}

pre-A2 reader rejection: json: unknown field "fold_record"
```

Every reader (thread/read, resume, fork, doctor) decodes the whole transcript in one pass and aborts on the first error, so ONE fold-record entry makes the **entire transcript unreadable** to a pre-A2 build — not just that turn. It is clean (a decode error, no crash) and self-healing: the same daemon restarted on this build declares the field and reads the file fine. This is the same one-way door every prior `schema.Turn` field addition opened. Option 2 (an ignore-list format) cannot fix daemons already shipped — they do not know the field either — so it would only help future readers, which option 1 already covers by restart. **Holding for Jesse's explicit ruling on the compat break.**

## Live-Seq threading — the count

The returned-Seq stamp threads through **3 write choke points** (`writeTranscriptLocked` / `writeTranscriptDurableLocked` / `writeTranscriptSyncedLocked`) and the history-append helpers that already hold the Seq in hand (`appendTurnAfterTranscriptWrite(Locked)`, `recordTurn`, `appendPairedTurnVia`, `attachTranscript`, `appendClientMutationTranscriptLocked`, `appendUserInputTurnRefusingPoison`, the skill-reload reminder append). The stamp lives only in those helpers; the rest is the mechanical `(int, error)` signature change fanning out to call sites: **16 production files** and **~59 test files**, uniform and behavior-preserving.

## Gates

title: refactor(native): rows are a projection of the model (D23c-2b)
body:
Slice c-2b of SDK-migration row D23 (docs/superpowers/plans/2026-09-12-sdk-migration.md), after c-2a (#1547, `d3c537e45`). The display rows become a projection of the package model: after every accepted frame the store publishes `capAndTruncate(projectConversation(applied))`, so a frame and a snapshot produce rows through the one projector and there is nothing for a row applier to disagree with.

## What the store does now

```ts
const applied = applyThreadNotification(state.conversation, n);
if (applied !== state.conversation) {
  set({ conversation: capAndTruncate(withPageHistory(state.conversation, projectConversation(applied))) });
}
// evener/thread/resync stays the authoritative refresh path; an item frame the
// reducer has no case for leaves the model untouched and asks for the canonical read.
```

The Q10 caps are one pure post-projection pass (`capAndTruncate` = `capItems` 500 rows, then `truncateItem` at 64 KiB with the marker). Because the bound is re-applied to whatever text a row carries, the truncation freeze is unnecessary: an oversized stream shows the same bounded prefix however much more arrives, and an authoritative short version is short again.

**Deleted from `mobile/src/state/conversation.ts`** (~1,200 lines): `projectSingleItem`, `decorateLifecycleItem`, `containingTurnStatus`, the cluster splicing (`findActivityTargetBy`/`findActivityTarget`/`findActivityTargetByIdentity`, `activityClusterSegments`, `mergeLiveActivityMembers`, `projectActivityMembers`, `replaceActivityTargetDetail`, `attachToSources`, `itemsAbsentFromSnapshot`), all seven row appliers with `publishModel`, `liveOwnedRevs`/`markLiveOwned`/`liveRevisionForItem`/`isLiveOwned`, `truncatedItemIds` with `truncateAndRecord`/`truncateAndRecordSingle`/`reconcileTruncationFrom`/`exceedsByteLimit`/`exceedsActivityDetailLimit`, the rehydrate live-ownership merge, and `getTruncatedItemIds` (interface + impl).

**Kept for D23d:** `pageOwnedIds` and the page prepend. The older pages live outside the model until D23d moves them in, so `withPageHistory` carries page-owned rows across every publish (and the rehydrate merge keeps the page's own cursor). `pruneEvictedIds` now prunes page ownership only.

**`mobile/src/conversation/project.ts`:** a `warning` item projects as the failure card its notice is (the reducer's `case "warning"` stamps `ItemModel.warning`); a reasoning row reads the per-`summaryIndex` chunks the model keeps (`joinedReasoningParagraphs`' rule, the same string[][] the web's think block renders); a question row on screen counts as a pending ask, so a live ask is answerable without waiting for a snapshot. `isActiveItem`, `activityState` and `clusterActivities` are private again, and `projectItemAttachments` with `inlineImageSrc`/`inputImage`/`outputImage` is deleted — the reducer resolves image sources now.

## Decision-2 behaviour deltas (what changes on the phone)

| Frame | Before (row appliers) | Now (projection of the model) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `item/agentMessage/reset` | blanked the row's markdown | removes the item, so the row goes; the restart streams from the `item/started` that follows |
| a delta naming no item in the model | requested a reread | ignored; the snapshot cut settles it |
| `item/toolOutput/delta` | required stored+incoming `callId` to match | routed by item id, as the wire routes it; the row keeps showing its own `callId` |
| a reasoning delta at a tool row (and the mirror) | requested a reread | invisible — the field it writes is not the field that row displays — and asks for nothing |
| `warning` with no active turn | appended a failure row | dropped (warnings are not transcript-persisted, so no snapshot would carry it) |
| ask_user `item/started`/`item/completed`, an unknown item type, a userMessage while an ask is pending | requested a reread | settled locally: tool row, question row + `askPending`, user row |
| a sparse assistant `item/completed` | re-projected the row from the sparse frame, blanking streamed text | keeps the streamed text (the model merged it) |
| a reasoning `item/completed` carrying its own text | replaced the row's output | the accumulated chunks stay (reducer's `mergeReasoning`); an item that streamed nothing shows its settled text |
| an item frame naming a turn the model does not have | inserted a row anyway | dropped — the wire opens a turn before the items in it |
| a live frame during a read | won over the snapshot that followed | the snapshot wins: the read response is ordered at the snapshot cut, so the frame is already in it |
| a live frame naming a row that exists only in an older page | updated that row | invisible until D23d moves the pages into the model |
| model text under deltas | frozen at 64 KiB per item id | rows bounded per publish; the model keeps the full text (#1535) |

## Mechanism → behaviour: every rewritten test

No test was dropped; each mechanism assertion became the visible outcome it stood for. The suite is 755 → 761 shared tests (conversation store + projector), with the ownership-set assertions replaced by row assertions.

| Old test (mechanism) | Now asserts (behaviour) |
| --- | --- |
| `item/started inserts/replaces` ×3 (row fixtures) | same rows, from wire fixtures on an open turn |
| `item/completed settles item`: cluster member update, later-member transcript identity, attachments | same rows and attachment ids, projected from two clustered tool items |
| `retains an omitted live-owned cluster during a held rehydrate` | `takes the reread's snapshot over a cluster the live frames built` |
| `keeps a failed member separate during a held rehydrate` ×2 | `commits the reread's own members, page history first` ×2 |
| `preserves a later member completion during a held rehydrate` | `carries a later member's completion into the cluster row` |
| `marks an activity item as completed/failed…` ×4 | one `it.each` over (exitCode, error) → row state |
| `2A: notification-path …family` ×2 | same family/label/callId assertions on the row |
| `preserves streamed reasoning text when sparse item/completed settles it` ×3 | unchanged (now proved through the projector) |
| `explicit (empty) text remains authoritative when reasoning completes` ×2 | `keeps the accumulated reasoning when the completion carries %s` ×2 + `shows the settled text of a reasoning item that streamed nothing` |
| `retains truncation ownership when sparse completion preserves output` | `bounds a reasoning row that streamed past the byte limit, and re-bounds it on every later frame` |
| `I4: delta targeting missing item triggers coalesced resync` | `ignores a delta targeting a missing item, without a reread` |
| `F7: ask_user started/completed schedules reread` ×2 | `projects a started ask_user as its question row / a completed one with askPending, without a reread` |
| `missing assistant delta / wrong-kind delta schedules reread`, `unrelated notification does NOT` | one `it.each`: `does not reread for %s` (three frames) + `rereads for an item frame the model has no rule for` |
| `Task 2A-Items: exact delta families` ×18 (A/B controlled-reread ownership + freeze proofs) | 10 rows: `leaves the row unchanged under %s` ×3, `appends to the row under %s` ×4, `keeps the tool row's own callId`, `commits the reread's rows when it %s` ×2 |
| `Fix round 1: per-item live ownership` ×9 and `Task 2A live-matrix: PAGE-RACE × live-ownership` ×7 | `the reread's snapshot decides the rows`: `shows the live change under $kind until the reread commits` ×3, `commits the reread's own X …` ×3, `drops X when the snapshot omits it` ×3, the two activity-delta rows, page history + cursor, cap trim, oversized→short |
| `Residual 2: live-owned item IDs` ×2 | `page history in front of the snapshot's rows` ×2 |
| `I4: question lifecycle` ×4 (reread-driven) | same rows, settled locally; `askPending` from the question row |
| `R2 ask reread racing page success` / `preserves a newer live version across a wire-id change` | driven by a resync; the snapshot's row commits |
| `R3 malformed/incomplete ask_user` ×2 | same conservative rows, read driven by a resync |
| `Task 2A-Cluster: live updates resolve clustered members` ×6 freeze cases | bounded-row assertions (`keeps a later clustered member bounded…`, `takes the reread's member…`, `shows a later member short again…`) |
| `Task 2A-Truncation residual` ×12 (`reconcileTruncationFrom`, identity freezes, superseded) | bound-follows-the-text assertions: bounded field, short completion, reread short, `C4 the cap shows the newest rows`, `protocol reset→start→delta` |
| `Task 2A-Truncation residual fix round 1` ×4 (`I2 rehydrate …`) | `commits the reread's row after %s lands mid-read` ×3 + `drops a row the reread omits…` |
| `fix round 2` ×4 (`M1 …` ownership) | `commits exactly the reread's rows when wire id and transcriptKey differ`, `M1 omission: a page brings a dropped row back short`, `M1 cap: the oldest row is trimmed when %s appends at 501` ×2 |
| `fix round 3` ×2 (member freezes) | member bounds, re-applied on every publish |
| `Plan3: getTruncatedItemIds` ×3 | `the byte bound follows the row's own text` ×2 (the accessor-only test is gone with the accessor) |
| `Task 2A-Items: unified truncation ownership` ×3 | `one byte bound for every row` ×3, on wire fixtures |
| `Task 2A-Cluster: sparse live items` ×2 (phantom rows for absent turns) | `shows no row for a started item when %s` ×2 |
| `F8 delta-after-marker`, `F12 genuine marker`, `split Unicode` | same outcomes, on wire fixtures (they had become vacuous behind `if (item?.kind …)` guards once rows came from the model) |
| `the model is live under the item frames (dual-write)` ×4 | `the model under the item frames is what the rows show` ×3 (the warning-drop case moved to F7) |
| `liveImages` ×3 (live image wins over an older snapshot) | the snapshot's image commits; the live change is asserted on screen first |

New projector tests (`mobile/src/conversation/project.test.ts`): warning → failure card (with and without a title), reasoning from chunks, reasoning fallback text, question row ⇒ `askPending`, malformed ask ⇒ no question row and `askPending` false.

## Gates (on the merged tree)

- `make test-native` — green: Metro iOS bundle exported, native 787/787 (81 files), shared 761/761, tsc, script imports
- `make lint-package-imports` — `PASS (1s)`
- `EVENER_GITLEAKS_REQUIRED=1 make secret-scan` — `PASS`; `gitleaks detect --no-git` over `mobile/src` and the changed native test — `no leaks found`
- root `go test -short -count=1 .` — `ok primeradiant.com/evener 23.665s`
- `make test-api-package` not run: the package is untouched (a reducer change would be a stop-and-ask; none was needed). No biome over `mobile/` or `mobile-native/` (#1157).

## Residuals

- `mobile-native/src/liveImages.test.ts` is in the diff: its three oracles encode the same live-wins-over-snapshot rule and had to invert with it.
- `reducer.mergeReasoning` keeps chunks seeded from an item's own text over a later `item/completed` that carries different text, so a settle cannot correct a reasoning row. The web reads the same chunks, so both hosts behave this way; worth a package decision rather than a native rule.
- A live frame cannot reach a row that exists only in an older page until D23d.
